page.layout: One block of running text in a single column on the right printed page, set well into the page; no running head, no page number, no catchword. Small marginal fragments at the right edge belong to the neighbouring page and are left out.

main_text.p: {Tycho} autem, etsi Anomaliam in Motu Sectionum Æquinoctialium concedat; causam tamen non addit, cur eam negligat; & opinari licet, quod Rei difficultate absterritus, suum 51 sec. in Fixis Annuum Motum, ad 4 saltem secula, valere voluerit: de cæteris Sententiam hanc ferens; Ep. Astr. pag. 45, quòd apparentis Octavæ Sphæræ Motus, exactam Cognitionem, vix ulli Mortalium absolutè perscrutabilem existimet.

Tertiò: non habuit rationem mutationis Eccentricitatis Solaris, inæqualisque Motus Apogæi: quæ duo evidentissimè conspicua sunt in Cælo, & ab omnibus Astronomis observata. Nam quia Ptolemæus eandem pœnè Eccentricitatem, & Apogeum retinuit, quod invenerat Hipparchus; non statim suspicari licet cum Tychone, Prog. Tom. 1. pag. 32. vel utriusque Observationi, vel alterius saltem eorum, errorem aliquem subesse, sed causa erit perspicua, si dicamus, Centrum Eccentrici in utriusque Observatione, æqualiter fere distitisse, à limite Maximæ Eccentricitatis, in parvo Circello, (juxta Theoriam Solis, in Progymnasmatibus D. Lansbergij, Cælestibus Phænomenis congruenter expressam) & 285 Annis, quot sunt inter Observationem Hipparchi & Ptolemæi; contrà Successionem Signorum in tantum delatum fuisse, quantum medij Apogei Linea, processerat in Signorum Consequentia. Inde enim factum necessariò, ut Apogæum verum, tempore Ptolemæi, eodem fere loco Sphærę Fixarum conspectum sit, quo tempore Hipparchi; & Ptolemæus non confidenter, ut vult Longimontanus Parte 2. Astr. Dan. pag. 48. sed secundum Rei veritatem, situm Apogei, suo seculo eundem retinuerit. Post Ptolemæum; Albategnius, Arzahel, Regiomontanus, Copernicus, D. Lansbergius, alijque; variabilem Eccentricitatem, & inæqualem Apogei progressum, deprehenderunt: nec quicquam causę superest, cur Tycho eam præterierit; nisi forte, quòd proprijs Observationibus nimium addictus, rejectis inventis aliorum;

page.notes: The first word "Tycho" is in italic and the line-initial letters are heavily set; the final line "rum;" stands alone at the right of the column. Several Greek-style symbols (astronomical signs) before "Ptolemæus" and "Albategnius" are not reproduced and were read as conventional marks. Some words were read with reduced confidence due to ink density, notably "Apogei" and "Lansbergij". No marginal notes are printed on this page.
